subject: Quality observability & canary / regression plan for AcmeHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oscar Low <oscar.low@acmehealth.com>, techops@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: quality monitoring expectations for Redwood integration

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we kick off the implementation, the platform team at AcmeHealth wants to lock down how we monitor prompt-level quality and detect regressions before they reach production. Specific asks:

- We need a recommended set of seed prompts for each clinical workflow (triage, patient messaging, discharge summaries).
- An eval harness we can run nightly against canary snapshots (and ideally a quick smoke test for pushes).
- Alerting thresholds so our PagerDuty doesn't flap on noisy drift.
- Clear canary/rollback guidance if model degradation is detected.

Can you share a proposed plan and who from Redwood will own the eval integration and ongoing tuning? We start smoke testing next Tuesday (6/2).

Attachments: example_user-flows.csv

Best,
Julia Park
Director, Product Ops — AcmeHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: quality monitoring expectations for Redwood integration

Thanks Julia — great summary and helpful timeline. High level plan below; attaching a short checklist and the eval template we typically use.

Summary plan (owners in parentheses):
1) Prompt set collection (Acme + CS): we will run a short workshop to refine seed prompts per workflow. Owner: Julia + Tessa (R: Tessa).
2) Eval harness integration (Redwood infra): we will wire Acme's test harness into our nightly CI to evaluate canary model snapshots using the agreed prompt sets and metrics. Owner: Marcus (R: Marcus).
3) Regression alerting (SLO leads): define metric thresholds (accuracy, hallucination score, domain-specific checks), set severity levels and PagerDuty filters to avoid noisy alerts. Owner: Hannah (R: Hannah).
4) Canary & rollback policy: we recommend a 2-step canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> full) with automatic rollback if key metrics breach thresholds for two consecutive runs. Documented runbook and playbook attached. Owner: Marcus + Hannah.

Immediate next steps for this week:
- Tessa: schedule a 60m prompt workshop with Acme (can do Monday or Tuesday).
- Marcus: confirm integration points for nightly harness (which endpoints, auth tokens, and expected payloads).
- Julia: share any existing golden responses or labeled examples you want included in the seed set.

Attachments: quality_eval_template.csv, canary_policy_v1.md

I'll be primary contact for escalation and will own the thresholds and alerting config. Marcus and Tessa will help with infra and prompt curation.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: quality monitoring expectations for Redwood integration

Looping in infra details. Julia — quick notes on how we'll integrate the eval harness:

- We'll spin up a dedicated nightly job in Redwood CI that hits a canary model snapshot endpoint we control. The job will run the prompt set, compute metrics (BLEU-like similarity for structured outputs, hallucination heuristics, and domain regex checks), and push results to the Acme shared Drive folder and to our monitoring dashboard.
- Auth: we'll use a scoped API key per Acme project; TechOps can rotate it via KMS.
- Time budget: each nightly run should complete within 45 minutes for the expected prompt volume; for faster smoke tests on deploys we'll run a reduced prompt subset (~30 prompts) that finishes <5 minutes.

I can take point on the integration and provide the harness doc. Tessa — please confirm the workshop slots, and Hannah I'll need the final list of metrics you want in the PagerDuty mapping.

Attachment: eval-harness-integration-guide.pdf

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: quality monitoring expectations for Redwood integration

Julia — I booked two slots for the prompt workshop: Monday 2026-05-31 10:00-11:00 PT and Tuesday 2026-06-01 15:00-16:00 PT. Please pick the one that works for your content team.

Workshop agenda (60m):
- 0–10m: goals and workflows (triage, messaging, discharge)
- 10–30m: collect representative prompts and golden responses
- 30–45m: label edge-case failure modes and expected tolerance
- 45–60m: finalize nightly vs. smoke prompt subsets and ownership

Action items for attendees: bring 10–20 real examples per workflow and any rejection/hallucination cases you've observed.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: quality monitoring expectations for Redwood integration

Hannah / team — Thanks, this looks good and clear. We confirm Monday 5/31 10:00 PT for the prompt workshop. We've pulled together 25 sample prompts for triage and 15 for patient messaging; attaching a small subset here as "golden_examples.csv".

Two quick questions before the workshop:
1) For the canary thresholds, can you share example numbers you typically use for a first-pass (so we can align internally)?
2) For PagerDuty, we prefer medium-severity alerts for a single-run breach and high-severity only after two consecutive runs fail. Is that something the Redwood alerting config supports?

We'll upload the full labeled set to the Drive link you shared tonight.

Best,
Julia
Director, Product Ops — AcmeHealth
Attachments: golden_examples.csv
